==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}}
From {{inh|en|enm|occupien}}, {{m|enm|occupyen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|occuper}}, from {{der|en|la|occupō|occupāre|t=to take possession of, seize, occupy, take up, employ}}, from {{m|la|ob||to, on}} + {{m|la|capiō||to take}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kap-<id:seize>||to seize, grab}}. {{doublet|en|occupate}}, now obsolete.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|ŏʹ-kyo͝o-pī|a=RP}} {{IPA|en|/ˈɒkjʊpaɪ/}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-occupy.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɑkjəpaɪ/|a=GenAm}}
* {{hyphenation|en|oc|cu|py}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|of time}} To take or use.
## To [[fill]].
##: {{ux|en|The film '''occupied''' three hours of my time.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=I corralled the judge, and we started off across the fields, in no very mild state of fear of that gentleman's wife, whose vigilance was seldom relaxed. And thus we came by a circuitous route to Mohair, the judge '''occupied''' by his own guilty thoughts, and I by others not less disturbing.}}
## {{senseid|en|keep busy}}To possess or use the time or capacity of; to engage the service of.
##: {{ux|en|The film '''occupied''' me for three hours.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''occupy''' myself with gardening for a few hours every day.}}
## To [[fill]] or [[hold]] (an official position or role).
##: {{ux|en|I '''occupy''' the post of deputy cat catcher.}}
## To hold the [[attention]] of.
##: {{ux|en|I '''occupied''' her friend while he made his proposal.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To take or use [[space]].
## To fill space.
##: {{ux|en|The historic mansion '''occupied''' two city blocks.}}
## To [[live]] or [[reside]] in.
##* {{RQ:Irving Tales of a Traveller|passage=The better apartments were already '''occupied'''.}}
##* {{RQ:Schuster Hepaticae|volume=V|page=vii|text=With fresh material, taxonomic conclusions are leavened by recognition that the material examined reflects the site it '''occupied'''; a herbarium packet gives one only a small fraction of the data desirable for sound conclusions. Herbarium material does not, indeed, allow one to extrapolate safely: what you see is what you get{{...}}}}
## {{lb|en|military}} To have, or to have taken, possession or control of (a territory).
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1940|journal=The China monthly review|volume=94-95|page=370|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=QqkTAAAAIAAJ&q=%22occupy+but+cannot+hold%22&dq=%22occupy+but+cannot+hold%22&hl=en&sa=X&ei=OB6HT4_zC4e68ASF1-jNCA&ved=0CDQQ6AEwAA
|passage=The Japanese can '''occupy''' but cannot hold, and what they can hold they cannot hold long, was the opinion of General Pai Chung-hsi, Chief of the General Staff of the Chinese Army, {{...}}}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1975|author=Esmé Cecil Wingfield-Stratford|title=King Charles and King Pym, 1637-1643|pageurl=http://books.google.com/books?ei=ex2HT9-GK5D69gTJqNjdCA&id=VCwqAAAAYAAJ&dq=%22occupied+but+could+not+hold%22&q=%22occupied+but+could%22#search_anchor|page=330
|passage=Rupert, with his usual untamable energy, was scouring the country — but at first in the wrong direction, that of Aylesbury, another keypoint in the outer ring of Oxford defences, which he '''occupied''' but could not hold.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1983|author=Arthur Keppel-Jones|title=Rhodes and Rhodesia: The White Conquest of Zimbabwe, 1884-1902|page=462
|passage=One of the rebel marksmen, who had taken up position on a boulder, was knocked off it by the recoil of his weapon every time he fired. Again the attack achieved nothing. Positions were '''occupied''', but could not be held.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1991|author=Werner Spies; John William Gabriel|title=Max Ernst collages: the invention of the surrealist universe|page=333
|passage=Germany '''occupied''' France for three years while France struggled to make payments that were a condition of surrender.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=John Michael Francis|title=Iberia and the Americas: Culture, Politics, and History|page=496
|passage=Spain '''occupied''', but could not populate, and its failure to expand Florida led Britain to consider the peninsula a logical extension of its colonial holdings.}}
## {{lb|en|surveying}} To place the [[theodolite]] or [[total station]] at (a point).
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To have [[sexual intercourse]] with.<ref>Sidney J. Baker, ''The Australian Language'', second edition, 1966.<!-- not that there's anything Australian about this sense, it was just what I had to hand --></ref>
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-2|II|iv|text=God's light, these villains will make the word as odious as the word ''''occupy''';' which was an excellent good word before it was ill sorted<!-- note: this line is missing from the Project Gutenberg edition, bowdlerized or whatever -->}}
#* '''1867''', {{w|Robert Nares}} ''A Glossary''
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To do business in; to busy oneself with.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Ezekiel|27|9|text=All the ships of the sea, with their mariners, were in thee<!--sic--> to '''occupy''' the merchandise.}}
#* '''1551''', {{w|Ralph Robinson (humanist)|Ralph Robinson}} (tr.), Sir {{w|Thomas More}}'s ''{{w|Utopia (book)|Utopia}}'' (in Latin), 1516
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To use; to expend; to make use of.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Exodus|38|24|text=all the gold that was '''occupied''' for the work}}
#* '''1551''', {{w|Ralph Robinson (humanist)|Ralph Robinson}} (tr.), Sir {{w|Thomas More}}'s ''{{w|Utopia (book)|Utopia}}'' (in Latin), 1516

====Conjugation====
{{en-conj|pres_3sg=occupies|pres_3sg_old=occupieth|pres_2sg_old=occupiest|past=occupied}}

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|to possess or use the time or capacity of}} {{l|en|employ}}, {{l|en|busy}}, {{l|en|exercise}} {{qualifier|formal}}
* {{sense|to have sexual intercourse with}} {{l|en|coitize}}, {{l|en|go to bed with}}, {{l|en|sleep with}}; see also [[Thesaurus:copulate with]]
